chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Hamam Abu Ali quoted on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, quoted on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, on the authority of Abil Muthanna an-Nakha'i, on the authority of Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Hussein, on the authority of his father Ali ibn Al-Hussein, on the authority of his father (peace be upon them both).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'How can a nation perish, which begins with me, Ali, and eleven of my progeny who are men of understanding, and ends with the Messiah, the son of Mary? However, anyone who does not belong to my nation, and I am not associated with, will perish.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the key figures that ensure the survival of the Muslim nation according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* establishes the concept of *Tahzib* (purification) of the nation through the continuous chain of authority starting with the Prophet, Ali, the eleven Imams, and concluding with Jesus (AS) at the end of time. It highlights the Shia belief in the infallible guidance of the Ahl al-Bayt as the guarantee against the spiritual corruption that leads to the perishing of those outside this lineage.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-33 Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani (ra) narrated that Muhammad ibn Hamam Abu Ali quoted on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Himyari, quoted on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, on the authority of Abil Muthanna an-Nakha’ee, on the authority of Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Hussein, on the authority of his father Ali ibn Al-Hussein (as), on the authority of his father (as)

that God’s Prophet (sw) said, “How can a nation that begins with me, Ali and eleven of my progeny who are all men of understanding and ends with the Messiah - the son of Mary - perish? However anyone who does not belong to my nation, and I am not associated with, will perish.”
